sections.title: Counting 1 to 20
sections.explanation: Numbers tell how many. We count objects in a line, clap as we say each number, and write the numeral beside a set of pictures.
points: Say numbers in order without skipping
Match groups of objects to the correct number

examples.title: Apples
examples.problem: Numair has 7 apples. What comes after 7?

examples.title: Fingers
examples.problem: Show 5 on one hand. What number is that?

sections.title: More, Less and Same
sections.explanation: Compare two groups. The group with extra objects has more; the other has less. Same means both groups match.
points: Line up objects to compare easily
Draw circles under each group to check

examples.title: Crayons
examples.problem: 3 crayons and 5 crayons — which has more?

examples.title: Biscuits
examples.problem: 4 and 4 biscuits — more, less or same?

sections.title: Addition within 10
sections.explanation: Addition finds the total. Put groups together and count all. The signs + and = help write number sentences.
points: Start with the larger number and count on

examples.title: Toys
examples.problem: 2 cars and 3 cars. How many in all?

sections.title: Subtraction within 10
sections.explanation: Subtraction finds how many are left. Take some away, or find the difference between two numbers.
points: Cross out pictures you take away
Keywords: left, remain, how many more
Check by adding the answer back

sections.title: Shapes Around Us
sections.explanation: Circles are round, squares have 4 equal sides, triangles have 3 sides, and rectangles have opposite sides equal.
points: Triangle: road signs, sandwiches cut that way

examples.title: Home
examples.problem: A round plate looks like which shape?

examples.title: Book
examples.problem: A book cover is usually a…

sections.title: Simple Patterns
sections.explanation: Patterns repeat in a rule. Spot what comes next by looking at colour, shape or size order.

sections.title: Long and Short
sections.explanation: We compare length by placing objects side by side. Longer sticks past the end; shorter ones stop earlier.
points: Hands and footsteps are informal measures

examples.title: Pencils
examples.problem: A new pencil and a stub — which is longer?

sections.title: Coins We Know
sections.explanation: India uses rupees. Small coins help us buy snacks. Counting coins builds number sense for shopping.
points: Know common coin values you see with family
Saving small amounts is a useful habit

examples.title: Shop
examples.problem: Two ₹1 coins make how many rupees?

sections.title: Day and Night Time Words
sections.explanation: Morning, afternoon, evening and night help us talk about when things happen in a day.

sections.title: Sorting and Pictographs Intro
sections.explanation: Sorting puts like things together. A simple pictograph uses pictures to show how many in each group.
points: Sort by colour, size or type
One picture can stand for one object

examples.title: Buttons
examples.problem: 3 red and 2 blue buttons — how many red?

questions.prompt: A square has how many equal sides?
How many fingers on one hand?
A triangle has how many sides?

tables.title: Multiplication Tables
tables.subtitle: Start with tables 1 to 5 — each table goes up to ×10. Say them aloud every day!
